label: Widening war
summary: The world drops to 35 as the Gulf conflict stops being a bilateral exchange and starts becoming a regional one. US Central Command completed a tenth consecutive night of strikes on Iran, hitting command centres, missile and drone sites and air defences, after Iranian missiles aimed at American positions in Jordan and Kuwait killed US service members and wounded others; Jordan intercepted three missiles, Kuwait reported shooting down ballistic missiles and drones, and President Masoud Pezeshkian called the fighting a 'full-scale war,' with Iranian authorities reporting at least 41 deaths and more than 400 wounded this month. Houthi-controlled Yemen then opened a second maritime front by declaring a blockade of Saudi Arabia, and two Dynacom tankers, the Kavomaleas and the Acheloos, were struck by unidentified projectiles off Oman. The one real opening was diplomatic: Pakistan and Qatar proposed a ten-day ceasefire to restore the Islamabad Memorandum, days after Washington said a negotiated end remained possible. Europe's war ground on: Russian cruise missiles set the Guinea-Bissau-flagged grain ship Golden Leo ablaze near Odesa, killing ten crew from India and Syria and taking the region's July death toll to 28, while Ukraine sent more than 400 drones at Moscow oblast overnight, wounding at least ten and hitting an oil depot. Economically the day was expensive: Trump signed an executive order imposing 50 percent tariffs on many Canadian goods in 30 days, Brent passed 90 dollars a barrel and US pump prices topped 4 dollars, with the S&P 500 easing 0.19 percent to 7,443.28 and the Dow shedding 307 points to 51,839.26. Roughly 850 to 1,000 Canadian wildfires pushed hazardous smoke over more than 20 US states and gave New York its second-worst smoke event in modern record; flash floods killed 20 in eastern Afghanistan with more than 100 missing, a hydropower tunnel collapsed on the Teesta in Sikkim killing 12, a ferry capsized in Guyana leaving 66 missing and a magnitude 5.5 quake near Huancayo, Peru killed six. Against that: Britain changed prime ministers without incident as Andy Burnham succeeded Keir Starmer, Sao Tome and Principe re-elected Carlos Vila Nova peacefully, a Saudi aid flight reached Khartoum, Spain closed a record-crowd World Cup by beating Argentina 1-0 in New Jersey to hold both men's and women's titles, and a mathematician disproved the long-standing Jacobian conjecture with the help of a large language model. Weighted: conflict 22x0.30 = 6.6, economy 38x0.20 = 7.6, climate 30x0.20 = 6.0, humanInterest 38x0.15 = 5.7, techProgress 60x0.15 = 9.0, total 34.9, rounding to 35 with no editorial adjustment.

drivers.headline: US Central Command completes a tenth consecutive night of strikes on Iran, targeting military command centres, missile and drone sites, maritime capabilities and air defences, hours after Trump warned Tehran would pay for the deaths of American service members; Iranian missiles aimed at US positions in Jordan wounded soldiers and damaged helicopters, Jordan intercepted three missiles and Kuwait reported downing ballistic missiles and drones, while President Masoud Pezeshkian called the fighting a 'full-scale war' and Iranian authorities reported at least 41 dead and over 400 wounded this month

Houthi-controlled Yemen declares a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia, citing a siege of nearly 12 years and opening a second front in the Gulf conflict, while Greek operator Dynacom Tankers reports that two of its ships, the Malta-flagged Kavomaleas and the Liberian-flagged Acheloos, were struck by unknown projectiles off the coast of Oman and Iran's Revolutionary Guard says two tankers exploded after transiting the Strait of Hormuz; US Central Command says it has redirected seven commercial vessels and disabled one since the blockade of Iranian ports resumed on 14 July

Pakistan and Qatar propose a ten-day ceasefire aimed at restoring the Islamabad Memorandum whose collapse triggered the current round of fighting, the first concrete mediation track since talks broke down over the Strait of Hormuz, and it follows US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's statement a day earlier that a diplomatic solution remains possible if Iran halts attacks on shipping in the strait

Russian cruise missiles set the Guinea-Bissau-flagged corn carrier Golden Leo ablaze near Odesa, killing nine crew members from India and Syria plus a maritime pilot with eight rescued, taking the Odesa region's July death toll to 28 amid up to 15 air raid alerts a day; Ukraine retaliated with more than 400 drones against Moscow and its surrounding region overnight, wounding at least ten people including a child and three Chinese citizens, striking an oil depot and logistics facilities in Moscow Oblast and hitting six Black Sea vessels, days after the largest ballistic missile barrage on Kyiv since the war began

Israeli air strikes killed at least nine Palestinians including three children in Gaza City on Saturday and hit tents sheltering displaced families in the south on Sunday night, with two more killed in strikes reported on Monday despite the October ceasefire under which more than 1,100 Palestinians have now died; separately about 40 Israeli settlers stormed a Palestinian village near Yatta in the occupied West Bank, setting fires at a mosque and buildings, while Hamas named Khalil al-Hayya as its new leader

President Trump signs an executive order imposing 50 percent tariffs on a wide range of Canadian goods, effective in 30 days with carve-outs for energy, potash and certain sectors, after blaming Ottawa for the wildfire smoke blanketing US cities; on the same day Brent crude passed 90 dollars a barrel and West Texas Intermediate reached 84.49 dollars on the Gulf fighting, while average US pump prices topped 4 dollars a gallon for the first time since 17 June

Smoke from roughly 850 to 1,000 active wildfires in Canada, including more than 180 in Ontario, and from fires in Minnesota pushed air quality to hazardous levels across the Upper Midwest, Great Lakes and Northeast, with alerts in more than 20 states and warnings in Chicago, Detroit, Columbus and Minneapolis; New York recorded its second-worst smoke event in modern history as tens of millions were advised to stay indoors

Heavy rains triggered flash floods across eastern Afghanistan, killing 20 people, injuring 80 and leaving more than 100 missing, while a suspected methane explosion collapsed part of a hydropower tunnel along the Teesta River in Sikkim, north-east India, killing 12 workers with 13 still unaccounted for

The Bundibugyo-virus Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo keeps accelerating, with confirmed cases past 2,400 and deaths approaching 1,000 barely two months in, making it the third-largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak on record; there is no licensed vaccine or treatment for the Bundibugyo strain, a newly affected health zone in Ituri brought the total to 47 across five provinces, and Canada imposed a temporary entry ban on foreign nationals who have visited the DRC in the previous 21 days, though remdesivir and MBP-134 trials are under way

Andy Burnham becomes the United Kingdom's seventh prime minister in a decade in an orderly constitutional handover, with Keir Starmer resigning outside Downing Street and travelling to Buckingham Palace before the King asked Burnham to form a government; the former Greater Manchester mayor called his appointment a 'circuit-breaker' and promised a new political and economic model built around a ten-year plan

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium to win the World Cup for a second time, Ferran Torres scoring in the 106th minute and Rodri taking the Golden Ball, making Spain the first nation to hold the men's and women's world titles simultaneously and extending their unbeaten run to 38 matches; a record-crowd tournament across Canada, Mexico and the United States closed without serious incident, with Argentina's Emiliano Martinez setting a final record of 11 saves

Mathematician Levent Alpöge presented a counterexample disproving the Jacobian conjecture for dimensions greater than two, developed with the assistance of a large language model, a rare case of an AI system contributing materially to the resolution of a decades-old open problem in pure mathematics, as researchers and companies gathered at the World Artificial Intelligence Conference in Shanghai
